title: Sort each commercial-math situation into the correct concept bin
instructions: Drag each card on the left into the bin that best describes the concept being applied. Watch for the keywords: 'cost' / 'sell' indicate profit/loss; 'marked' / 'discount' indicate discount; 'principal' / 'rate' / 'flat' indicate simple interest; 'compounded' indicates compound interest.

bins.name: Profit / Loss
bins.description: Profit / loss percent computed on cost price.

bins.name: Discount
bins.description: Discount applied to the marked price to give the selling price.

bins.name: Simple Interest
bins.description: Flat interest computed on the original principal each year.

bins.name: Compound Interest
bins.description: Interest added to the principal each period; grows exponentially.

items.name: An item bought for ₹500 is sold for ₹560
items.explanation: CP and SP given; the question is about profit (12 %).

items.name: A trader sells at a 15 % loss on cost price
By selling 12 oranges for ₹100 a vendor loses 4 %
items.explanation: Loss expressed as % of cost — profit/loss problem.

items.name: A bag is marked ₹600 and sold after a 10 % reduction
Two successive discounts of 10 % and 20 % on a marked TV
Shopkeeper marks 25 % above cost and gives 20 % off
₹2000 lent at 8 % p.a. for 3 years (flat)
items.explanation: 'Flat' or single rate p.a. → simple interest.
